title: Oath and Sigil
premise: Ansel Ishikawa survives in the walled city of Vell by stealing memories and selling them as charms, keeping her own past locked away. When a dying courier forces a map into her hands—a map to the Door of Thirteenth Moon, the last exit from Cael Sarn, a country erased from history—she becomes hunted by the Ministry of Unmaking, which erases people who remember too much. Pursued by a Ministry hunter who wears her stolen memories like armor, Ansel gathers a ragged company of the forgotten and follows the map through drowned villages and memory-haunted ruins toward a border that only exists for those willing to claim their true names. At the Door she must choose: pass through alone and free, or stay to break the Ministry's sigil and restore her country at the cost of her anonymity—and possibly her life.
about_author: Wendell Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a government basement before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about ordinary people trapped inside systems that would prefer they not exist.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Things
chapters.summary: Ansel works the night market of Vell, lifting memories from drunk merchants and pressing them into wax charms. POV: Ansel. Establishes her rules—never steal grief, never steal twice from one person—and her loneliness beneath the charm of competence.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Threshold
chapters.summary: A bleeding man collapses into Ansel's cellar hideout, presses a folded map into her hand, and dies whispering that the moon is wrong. POV: Ansel. Fear and reluctant responsibility; she realizes his death-memory is already bleeding into her.

chapters.title: What the Ministry Burns
chapters.summary: Ministry inspectors sweep the market, burning charms and questioning sellers. Ansel watches her livelihood turn to ash and understands the map has marked her. POV: Ansel. The beat is the collapse of her careful invisibility.

chapters.title: The Hunter Who Wears My Face
chapters.summary: Introducing Corvane, a Ministry hunter whose stolen memories include fragments of Ansel's own childhood. POV: Corvane. He hunts her almost tenderly; the emotional beat is unsettling intimacy between predator and prey.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Ansel deciphers the map with help from Osk, a blind letter-carver, learning the Door opens only when the thirteenth moon completes its cycle—weeks away. POV: Ansel. Dread mixed with the first flicker of purpose.

chapters.title: The Drowned Village of Merrowgate
chapters.summary: Ansel flees the city walls into a village half-sunk by the Ministry's rewriting, where residents remember two contradictory histories. POV: Ansel. Grief for a country no one is allowed to mourn.

chapters.title: Company of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: She gathers unlikely allies: Osk, a deserter named Brava, and a child called Pip who remembers everything he shouldn't. POV: rotating ensemble. Warmth and friction as strangers become something like family.

chapters.title: Charms and Confessions
chapters.summary: Around a fire, each companion trades a true memory as payment for passage—an echo of Ansel's trade, but freely given. POV: Ansel. Vulnerability; she refuses to share hers and feels the cost of that refusal.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corvane interrogates captured charm-sellers, assembling a portrait of Ansel from other people's memories of her. POV: Corvane. His certainty begins to crack as the fragments contradict the Ministry's story.

chapters.title: The Bridge That Isn't There
chapters.summary: The company crosses a bridge that exists only in collective memory, held up by shared belief. Pip nearly falls when he doubts. POV: Brava. Awe and terror; faith as literal architecture.

chapters.title: Sigilwork
chapters.summary: Osk reveals the map is also a sigil—the Ministry's seal on the country itself—and that breaking it requires a name freely surrendered at the Door. POV: Osk. Revelation reframes the journey as sacrifice, not escape.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: Brava, offered amnesty for the group's capture, leads them into an ambush. Ansel saves Pip but loses the map. POV: Brava. Shame and desperation; betrayal born of love, not malice.

chapters.title: Memory of Water
chapters.summary: Mapless, Ansel navigates by the dead courier's memory still lodged in her mind, reliving his final journey. POV: Ansel. She grieves him properly for the first time; the dead man becomes her guide.

chapters.title: The Ministry's Kindness
chapters.summary: Captured briefly, Ansel is shown a vision of a painless, memoryless life the Ministry offers all citizens. POV: Ansel. Temptation; she nearly says yes before recognizing erasure dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: What Corvane Forgot
chapters.summary: Corvane finds Ansel alone but cannot strike—her stolen childhood memories surface, revealing he was once her neighbor, unmade for remembering her. POV: Corvane. His loyalty shatters; hunter becomes questioner.

chapters.title: The Ruin of Cael Sarn
chapters.summary: The company reaches the capital's ruin, where buildings stand only as outlines and names are scrawled on doorframes by pilgrims. POV: Ansel. Devastating beauty; mourning made communal.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Rising
chapters.summary: The false thirteenth moon rises, and the Door appears—a seam of light in the ruin's heart. The Ministry arrives in force. POV: ensemble. Tension peaks; every debt comes due.

chapters.title: The Price of the Door
chapters.summary: At the threshold, Ansel learns passage demands a true name surrendered forever. She offers hers—and then, seeing the sigilwork, understands she could instead spend it breaking the seal. POV: Ansel. The central choice crystallizes.

chapters.title: Breaking the Seal
chapters.summary: With Corvane holding off the Ministry and Osk carving the counter-sigil, Ansel surrenders her name into the seal, shattering it. Memories flood back into the land. POV: Ansel. Climax: self-annihilation as an act of creation.

chapters.title: The Country Remembers
chapters.summary: Cael Sarn reconstitutes around them—color returning, the drowned rising—but Ansel stands nameless and half-faded at its center. POV: ensemble. Triumph shadowed by loss; the world saved, the self spent.

chapters.title: A Name Given Back
chapters.summary: Pip, Brava, and the returned citizens speak Ansel's name aloud, refusing to let the Ministry's logic claim her; memory given freely restores what was taken. POV: Ansel. Grace—identity rebuilt not in secrecy but in community.

chapters.title: Oath and Sigil
chapters.summary: Months later, Vell's walls are open and charms are legal again. Ansel keeps a small shop selling nothing but honest keepsakes, while Corvane, pardoned, delivers letters. POV: Ansel. Quiet resolution: survival's price paid, and worth it.
